claims.text: Bismuth quadruple therapy for 14 days, the best initial therapy where clarithromycin resistance is > 15% or unknown:
claims.quote: Quadruple therapy is the best initial therapy in areas where the clarithromycin resistance rate is > 15% or in patients in whom microbial resistance data are not available and is recommended in both the European guidelines (4) and in the ACG guidelines (1). In quadruple therapy, the following oral medications are given for 14 days

claims.text: a PPI twice a day (esomeprazole 40 mg once a day)
claims.quote: A proton pump inhibitor (lansoprazole 30 mg 2 times a day, omeprazole 20 mg 2 times a day, pantoprazole 40 mg 2 times a day, rabeprazole 20 mg 2 times a day, or esomeprazole 40 mg once a day)

claims.text: + bismuth subsalicylate 524 mg 4 times a day
claims.quote: Bismuth subsalicylate 524 mg 4 times a day

claims.text: Clarithromycin triple therapy, only where clarithromycin resistance is known to be < 15% and with no previous macrolide exposure:
claims.quote: In regions where H. pylori clarithromycin resistance is known to be < 15% and in patients with no previous history of macrolide exposure, triple therapy with the following oral medications for 14 days remains an initial treatment option

claims.text: + amoxicillin 1 g twice a day (or metronidazole 250 mg 4 times a day)
claims.quote: Amoxicillin 1 g 2 times a day or metronidazole 250 mg 4 times a day

claims.text: If quadruple therapy fails: low-dose rifabutin + amoxicillin + a PPI,
claims.quote: If quadruple therapy fails, the European guidelines suggest dual therapy with a high-dose PPI and amoxicillin or triple therapy with a PPI, amoxicillin, and a fluoroquinolone (4). There is a high prevalence of fluoroquinolone resistance in the United States, so this strategy may not be applicable there. Triple therapy with low-dose rifabutin, amoxicillin, and a PPI is an alternative
An alternative is dual therapy with vonoprazan and amoxicillin, which is effective in patients with clarithromycin-resistant strains of H. pylori

claims.text: ACG says not clarithromycin triple therapy.
claims.quote: The ACG guidelines recommend that triple therapy with clarithromycin not be used if quadruple therapy fails
